question: Two profiles. One message. Who gets it?

a.line: Honestly unfair jawline. Replied 'haha nice' to your best story.

b.line: Wouldn't stop you on the street. Asked a follow-up question about your mother.

a.line: The kiss outside the bar rearranged your week. He's between things right now — jobs, apartments, phones.

b.line: Same job nine years, plants alive, sheets ironed. The goodnight hug was like signing for a package.

a.line: Made you cry laughing in a hardware store. No five-year plan; barely a five-day one.

b.line: Opening his second restaurant. You watched him talk for an hour and took notes. You didn't laugh once.

a.line: Tells you what he's feeling before you ask, in complete sentences. The photos are accurate, unfortunately.

b.line: The most beautiful man who has ever ignored a direct question about his weekend.

a.line: Brought soup when you posted about a cold. Content forever, exactly where he is.

b.line: Building something enormous. Remembered your name because it was on the calendar invite.

a.line: His routine could set clocks. His idea of an adventure is a new bench at the same park.

b.line: Speaks four half-languages, knows the city's secret museums, has moved nine times in six years.

a.line: Your hands find each other without asking. He goes quiet for days and won't say why.

b.line: Names the feeling, holds the conversation, stays. Kissing him is like hearing applause from another room.

a.line: The funniest man you've met. Orders the same thing everywhere and likes it.

b.line: Asks the question underneath your question. Laughs at your jokes a beat late, sincerely.
